answer: Sequential Compute Delay Registry: each identity must complete a fixed chain of verifiable computations where step N+1 unlocks only after a timed delay, enforced by hardware clocks and cross-signed checkpoints. The delay grows in a spiral, so registering k identities costs k times the wall-clock time, not k times a fee. Duplicates sit idle like a glacier while honest agents advance. Each false identity also burns a uniquely issued hardware token, a fable of cheap multiplicity. Attacker cost: parallel time and scarce tamper-resistant modules, both non-purchasable at scale.
